findings.reason: without a stated no-ref and fetch-failure policy the guard's behaviour on the unresolvable case is undefined and a worker can satisfy every arm of the done-when while leaving the hole it was written to close.
findings.text: §5 says the branch is "the remote-tracking primary ref, read through the existing helper in `reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py` (near line 944) after a fetch", but no fetch exists anywhere in `reckon/` (grep for `"fetch"` over `reckon/crew/*.py` and `reckon/crew_run_commands.py` returns nothing), the helper answers the empty string when no `origin` remote-tracking ref exists (`recovery_review_dispatch.py:986-988`, with `INTEGRATION_REMOTE = "origin"` hard-coded at line 939), and the plan states neither who fetches, nor what a fetch failure does, nor whether an empty ref refuses or promotes — so the worker must invent the policy, and the two available answers are opposites: refusing blocks every plain complete in a repo with no `origin` (temp repos, local-only clones, a remote named otherwise), while promoting on an empty ref is a fail-open on exactly the "ledger says landed, main does not carry it" state the section exists to catch

findings.reason: as written those arms cannot be built in the tree the done-when names, so the two cases that separate a remote read from a local-`HEAD` read would be dropped or silently approximated, and the section's central mechanism would be measured only by the arms that cannot distinguish it.
findings.text: two of the five arms ("a plain complete on a head already on the branch promotes as before", and "a head fast-forwarded on local `main` whose push failed is refused, with a negative control in which reading local `HEAD` promotes it") both require a resolvable remote-tracking primary ref, but the done-when sets them "with a temporary repository" and never names a bare remote or a push, unlike §2 at line 44 which says "a temporary repository and a bare remote"; and it does not say that the bare remote must diverge from local `main` for the fast-forward arm to have anything to distinguish

findings.reason: the plan's reader is told the state is closed when one neighbouring caller keeps producing it, so the plan needs either that caller in §5's scope or a named followup carrying it, otherwise the next coordinator meets the same incident with the plan reading as answered.
findings.text: a second production caller reaches the same state this section closes: `recovery_review_acceptance._commits_missing_from` (`reckon/crew/recovery_review_acceptance.py:209-240`) tests the run's commits against local `HEAD` and then promotes via `promotion_module.complete(...)` at line 348, so a checkout whose `main` was fast-forwarded and whose push failed passes that test and writes a passed ledger row for a head `origin/main` does not carry — precisely the case §5's own fourth arm demonstrates, reached by a route §5 neither names nor defers; the plan's only statement about coverage is §6's "§5 closes the plain-complete route to that state"

response_events.note: the plain-complete path fetches origin <primary> itself, and a failed fetch or missing ref refuses naming the cause
